subject: Inference stress orchestration & MAP: scheduling test windows and success criteria
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lewis <sam@dataforge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: initial ask — test env access + timing for perf run

Hi Sam,

Thanks again for the time last week. As discussed in the MAP, the last gating item before we can complete the contract is a short, scoped inference stress run that validates latency, TTFT, throughput, and concurrency behavior for the two primary workloads you described (single-turn generation and streaming chat).

To keep the window narrow and actionable, can you confirm the following by EOD Wednesday so we can book Redwood Dedicated capacity:
- Test environment hostname / IP range and whether it is accessible from our Redwood private pilot (we prefer a peered VPC).
- Service account or API key for the test harness (read-only tokens OK, please note expiry).
- Preferred 2-hour load windows (we will propose two options and pick one).
- Any SLOs you already consider critical (p50/p95 latency goals, max sustained concurrency).

I've attached a short spec that lists the metrics we'll capture and the synthetic traffic profiles we plan to run. We will provide a short mutual action checklist once windows are set.

Thanks —
Kimberly

[Attachment: inference_test_spec.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)]

From: Sam Lewis <sam@dataforge.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: DataForge SRE <sre@dataforge.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP: initial ask — test env access + timing for perf run

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick answers:
- Test env: staging-api.dataforge.com (10.44.12.0/24) — we can open a peering connection to your VPC for a limited window.
- API key: I created a scoped key (test-run) that expires 2026-07-01; key: DF-TEST-2a9f (we'll send via secure channel separately).
- Windows: PDT windows we can support: 2026-06-22 02:00–04:00 or 2026-06-23 20:00–22:00. Prefer the 22nd if you need daytime overlap.
- SLOs: internal goal is p95 < 450ms for single-turn, TTFT < 300ms median for streaming start; throughput: sustain 120 req/s for the short generation profile for 10m bursts, and concurrency up to 400 active streams with graceful shedding.

I'll loop in our SRE for peering and key handoff.

—Sam

On attachments: we don't need the entire spec but anything that lists payload sizes and sequence lengths helps us size the infra on our side.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lewis <sam@dataforge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: initial ask — test env access + timing for perf run

Thanks Sam — that's perfect.

Quick follow-ups:
- We will request a temporary VPC peering; can your SRE confirm the CIDR we should expect for the peered interface? We will drop routes after the window.
- Attached is our traffic matrix (small/medium/large payloads) and the exact telemetry we will collect: p50/p95/p99 latency by token boundary, TTFT (time-to-first-token), token throughput (tokens/s), and memory/KV cache hit ratios.
- Our proposed canonical success criteria for the MAP perf gate:
  * Single-turn p95 <= 550ms under 120 RPS sustained for 10m bursts (accept within 10% of your internal SLO)
  * Streaming TTFT median <= 350ms and start token p95 <= 600ms at 400 concurrent streams
  * No unrecoverable OOMs or >1% error rate on inference requests during the window

Can you confirm that we can use the API key for internal Redwood test harnesses (k6 + custom stream harness) and that the key is allowed for at least 24h prior to the run for smoke tests? If yes we'll schedule a smoke run 24h prior and then the main 2-hour run.

Proposed scheduling: smoke window 2026-06-21 23:00–23:30 PDT, main window 2026-06-22 02:00–04:00 PDT. Please let us know conflicts.

[Attachment: load_schedule.csv (CSV, 3KB)]

—Kimberly

From: DataForge SRE <sre@dataforge.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Sam Lewis <sam@dataforge.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 08:09:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP: initial ask — test env access + timing for perf run

Hi team,

We can handle peering for the 22nd window. CIDR for peering will be 10.100.0.0/24 on our side. We'll open firewall rules for your Redwood pilot IPs once we receive the peering request from your infra team.

Key note: test key DF-TEST-2a9f will be rotated the morning of the 21st; please coordinate smoke tests after rotation (we will provide final key in secure vault). No problem to allow read-only quotas for your k6 harness.

Also: we prefer that long-running concurrency tests be limited to 60-minute stretches inside the window and that you ramp in/out over 5–10 minutes to avoid noisy neighbor impact on our production-similar services.

Thanks,
Ravi (DataForge SRE)

[Attachment: none]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: infra/keys checklist + runbook items

Kim —

We can own the peering request and will spin up the Dedicated pool during the windows you listed. Quick notes from infra:
- Requesting peering today (10.100.0.0/24). ETA for route propagation: ~2 hours after acceptance.
- We'll provision a k6 cluster for load generation (50 agents) and a separate streaming harness that emulates client WebSockets.
- Logs/metrics: we'll push token-level traces and client-side observed TTFT into the MAP dashboard. Please confirm which retention you want for traces (default 7d).

Plan to run the smoke tests on 2026-06-21 23:15 PDT (30m) and main on 2026-06-22 02:00–03:00 PDT (ramped to full concurrency for 60m). That aligns with DataForge SRE request to keep long concurrency inside 60 minutes.

—Aditya

On Tue, Jun 16, 2026 at 12:22 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm that we can use the API key for internal Redwood test harnesses (k6 + custom stream harness) and that the key is allowed for at least 24h prior to the run for smoke tests?

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Sam Lewis <sam@dataforge.com>, Ravi <sre@dataforge.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: final schedule and acceptance checklist (confirmed)

Sam / Ravi —

Thank you — this confirms the MAP perf gate schedule. Recap and acceptance criteria to finalize the contract side:
- Smoke run: 2026-06-21 23:15–23:45 PDT (k6 + streaming smoke, verify key and routes).
- Main run: 2026-06-22 02:00–03:00 PDT (ramp 10m, 60m sustained concurrency at 400 streams, ramp down 5m).
- Success criteria (final):
  * Single-turn p95 <= 550ms at 120 RPS bursts
  * Streaming TTFT median <= 350ms and p95 start token <= 600ms at concurrency target
  * Error rate < 1% and no OOMs; system gracefully sheds beyond capacity with <5% increased p95

Post-run deliverables (within 48h): consolidated perf report (p50/p95/p99 latency curves, TTFT distributions, token/s throughput, any regression notes), the MAP checklist sign-off, and a suggested config for production routing based on observed batch/cache behavior.

I'll keep the DocuSign routing paused pending a passed perf gate. If anything blocks us during smoke, please flag immediately in this thread and we will triage.

Best,
Kimberly
